I haven't changed anything since last time. The one failing test can't be made to pass without breaking the spec, so I left the implementation as it was.

`test_identifiers_are_lowercased` asserts that `tokenize("select Name from Users")` yields `name` and `users`. In the same file, `test_keywords_normalized_identifiers_preserved` asserts that the identical input yields `Name` and `Users`. These two cannot both pass.

The spec says identifiers keep their case:
- The module docstring says "kept exactly as written", and so does `Token` in `types.py`.
- `test_integration__keywords_case_insensitive_names_case_sensitive.py` runs `select Name from Users` and expects the result column to be `["Name"]`. It also expects `SELECT name FROM Users` to raise an error.

If I lowercased identifiers, I would fix the failing test. I would also break `test_keywords_normalized_identifiers_preserved` and that integration test, and it would violate the documented behavior. I won't do that just to turn the validator green.

The fix is outside what I'm allowed to change. `test_identifiers_are_lowercased` is almost certainly a stray or incorrect test. It needs to be deleted or corrected in `tests/test_tokenizer.py`. That file is on my allowed list but marked read-only by the task rules, so I haven't touched it. If you want me to remove that test, tell me and I'll do it. Otherwise whoever owns the test file should.

The other 22 tests pass.
